papers.title: Biologic complications and implant survival rates associated with implant-supported fixed complete dental prostheses. A clinical study with a mean 29-month follow-up from implant placement.
papers.abstract: STATEMENT OF PROBLEM: Prospective clinical data evaluating peri-implant biologic complications and marginal bone level changes associated with metal-acrylic resin implant-supported fixed complete dental prostheses (IFCDPs) using standardized clinical and radiographic protocols are limited. PURPOSE: The purpose of this prospective clinical study was to assess implant survival rates and biologic complications associated with IFCDPs after a mean observation period of 29 months from implant placement and 16 months from prosthesis delivery. The secondary aim was to identify risk factors of biologic complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Edentulous individuals in at least 1 arch, seeking treatment with fixed implant prostheses, were enrolled. Participants received 4 to 5 implants either in the maxilla or the mandible and were immediately loaded with a conversion prosthesis. Upon implant osseointegration, the definitive metal-acrylic resin prostheses were fabricated and delivered. Clinical peri-implant parameters, marginal bone level (MBL) changes, and biologic complications, including inflammation or overgrowth of the soft tissues, peri-implant mucositis, and peri-implantitis, were evaluated. Data were compared between anterior implants with laser-microgrooved and nonlaser-microgrooved abutments. RESULTS: Thirty-one participants were enrolled (mean age 61.60 ±10.50, 13 women). Implant survival was 99.26% at 29.4 ±12.20 months from implant placement. The implant-level incidence of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis was 90.1% and 9.9%, respectively, at 24 months. The incidence of inflammation under the prostheses and soft tissue overgrowth was 50% and 30%, respectively, at 24 months. Overall mean MBL remained coronal to the implant platform at all study visits and relatively stable over time. CONCLUSIONS: Implants supporting IFCDPs exhibited high survival rate, low rates of biologic complications such as peri-implantitis, and minimal MBL changes over time.

papers.title: Crab Shell Inspired Chitin/β-Tricalcium Phosphate Screws as Orthopedic Implants.
papers.abstract: Resorbable fracture fixation materials are currently gaining widespread attention due to their ability to avoid the second surgery and stress shielding. Inspired by the structure of the crab shell, herein, we propose high-strength resorbable screws composed of β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) and chitin as orthopedic implants. The incorporation of β-TCP into the chitin matrix not only improved the mechanical performance of the screws but also endowed them with osteogenic activity. The resulting chitin/β-TCP screws exhibited high flexural strength (up to 297 MPa) and tensile strength (up to 257 MPa), comparable to cortical bone. The chitin/β-TCP screws had favorable biocompatibility in vitro, which effectively promoted the adhesion of BMSCs and the expression of osteogenesis-related genes (RUNX2 and OCN), thereby facilitating bone healing. Importantly, the in vivo assessment of the rat femoral condyle indicated that the chitin/β-TCP screws were firmly fixed within the bone tunnel without inflammatory response and promoted the formation of new bone tissue during degradation. This work provides a biomimetic strategy for designing polysaccharide-based screws with significant potential applications in fracture internal fixation and anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
